title: Same push, two models

readouts.v: {model==0 ? "Economy K: Keynesian AS" : "Economy C: classical (vertical LRAS)"}

predict.q: Government spending rises: AD shifts right by the same amount in two economies. Economy K: deep recession, on the flat part of Keynesian AS. Economy C: already at full employment, in the vertical-LRAS model. What happens to each in the long run?

options.s: In both, real output rises for good and the price level hardly changes
options.fb: In C there is no spare capacity: once wages catch up, the extra demand only raises prices.

options.s: In K, real output rises with little change in the price level; in C, only the price level ends up higher
options.fb: K uses idle resources: more output at the same price level. In C, wages catch up, SRAS shifts back and output returns to Yfe at a higher price level.

options.s: In both, only the price level ends up higher; real output is unchanged
options.fb: In K there is lots of spare capacity, so firms can produce more without raising prices.

options.s: In K, only the price level ends up higher; in C, real output rises for good
options.fb: This swaps the models. Spare capacity is in K; full employment and flexible wages are in C.

task: Switch the model and move the AD slider; in C, also move the time slider to 12.

target.do: Shift AD right in both models; in C, move time to 12 quarters. Then press Check.

takeaway: Where the economy starts, and how flexible wages are, decide whether more AD buys output or only higher prices.
